guided.title: Missing days
guided.prompt: Print `order days: <n>`, `calendar days: <m>` (days from the first to the last order date inclusive) and `days with no orders: <m - n>`.
guided.starter:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd


def make_model():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
    customers = pd.DataFrame({
        "customer_id": np.arange(1, 41),
        "customer_name": [f"Customer {i:02d}" for i in range(1, 41)],
        "country": rng.choice(["UK", "Germany", "France", "Spain"], size=40),
        "segment": rng.choice(["Consumer", "Corporate", "Small Business"], size=40, p=[0.5, 0.3, 0.2]),
    })
    names = ["Desk", "Chair", "Bookcase", "Laptop", "Monitor", "Phone", "Notebook", "Pen Set", "Stapler", "Printer", "Lamp", "Cabinet"]
    categories = ["Furniture", "Furniture", "Furniture", "Technology", "Technology", "Technology",
                  "Office Supplies", "Office Supplies", "Office Supplies", "Technology", "Furniture", "Furniture"]
    products = pd.DataFrame({
        "product_id": np.arange(1, 13),
        "product_name": names,
        "category": categories,
        "unit_cost": rng.integers(5, 120, size=12),
    })
    sales = pd.DataFrame({
        "order_id": np.arange(1001, 1401),
        "order_date": pd.Timestamp("2025-01-01") + pd.to_timedelta(rng.integers(0, 365, 400), unit="D"),
        "customer_id": rng.integers(1, 41, 400),
        "product_id": rng.integers(1, 13, 400),
        "quantity": rng.integers(1, 8, 400),
    })
    cost = products.set_index("product_id")["unit_cost"]
    sales["unit_price"] = (cost[sales["product_id"]].to_numpy() * (1.3 + 0.5 * rng.random(400))).round(2)
    sales = sales.sort_values(["order_date", "order_id"]).reset_index(drop=True)
    dates = pd.date_range("2025-01-01", "2025-12-31", freq="D")
    calendar = pd.DataFrame({
        "date": dates,
        "year": dates.year,
        "quarter": dates.quarter,
        "month_number": dates.month,
        "month_name": dates.strftime("%B"),
    })
    return sales, customers, products, calendar


def validate_date_table(cal, sales_dates):
    dates = cal["date"]
    return {
        "unique": bool(dates.is_unique),
        "no blanks": bool(dates.notna().all()),
        "contiguous": bool((dates.sort_values().diff().dropna() == pd.to_timedelta(1, unit="D")).all()),
        "covers sales": bool(sales_dates.min() >= dates.min() and sales_dates.max() <= dates.max()),
    }

sales, customers, products, calendar = make_model()
sales = sales.assign(revenue=sales["quantity"] * sales["unit_price"])

Calendar =
ADDCOLUMNS (
    CALENDAR ( DATE ( 2024, 1, 1 ), DATE ( 2026, 12, 31 ) ),
    "year", YEAR ( [Date] ),
    "quarter", QUARTER ( [Date] ),
    "month_number", MONTH ( [Date] ),
    "month_name", FORMAT ( [Date], "MMMM" )
)

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd


def make_model():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
    customers = pd.DataFrame({
        "customer_id": np.arange(1, 41),
        "customer_name": [f"Customer {i:02d}" for i in range(1, 41)],
        "country": rng.choice(["UK", "Germany", "France", "Spain"], size=40),
        "segment": rng.choice(["Consumer", "Corporate", "Small Business"], size=40, p=[0.5, 0.3, 0.2]),
    })
    names = ["Desk", "Chair", "Bookcase", "Laptop", "Monitor", "Phone", "Notebook", "Pen Set", "Stapler", "Printer", "Lamp", "Cabinet"]
    categories = ["Furniture", "Furniture", "Furniture", "Technology", "Technology", "Technology",
                  "Office Supplies", "Office Supplies", "Office Supplies", "Technology", "Furniture", "Furniture"]
    products = pd.DataFrame({
        "product_id": np.arange(1, 13),
        "product_name": names,
        "category": categories,
        "unit_cost": rng.integers(5, 120, size=12),
    })
    sales = pd.DataFrame({
        "order_id": np.arange(1001, 1401),
        "order_date": pd.Timestamp("2025-01-01") + pd.to_timedelta(rng.integers(0, 365, 400), unit="D"),
        "customer_id": rng.integers(1, 41, 400),
        "product_id": rng.integers(1, 13, 400),
        "quantity": rng.integers(1, 8, 400),
    })
    cost = products.set_index("product_id")["unit_cost"]
    sales["unit_price"] = (cost[sales["product_id"]].to_numpy() * (1.3 + 0.5 * rng.random(400))).round(2)
    sales = sales.sort_values(["order_date", "order_id"]).reset_index(drop=True)
    dates = pd.date_range("2025-01-01", "2025-12-31", freq="D")
    calendar = pd.DataFrame({
        "date": dates,
        "year": dates.year,
        "quarter": dates.quarter,
        "month_number": dates.month,
        "month_name": dates.strftime("%B"),
    })
    return sales, customers, products, calendar


def validate_date_table(cal, sales_dates):
    dates = cal["date"]
    return {
        "unique": bool(dates.is_unique),
        "no blanks": bool(dates.notna().all()),
        "contiguous": bool((dates.sort_values().diff().dropna() == pd.to_timedelta(1, unit="D")).all()),
        "covers sales": bool(sales_dates.min() >= dates.min() and sales_dates.max() <= dates.max()),
    }

sales, customers, products, calendar = make_model()
sales = sales.assign(revenue=sales["quantity"] * sales["unit_price"])

cal = calendar.assign(
    fiscal_year=calendar["year"] + (calendar["month_number"] >= 4).astype(int),
    fiscal_month=(calendar["month_number"] - 4) % 12 + 1,
)
cal["fiscal_quarter"] = (cal["fiscal_month"] - 1) // 3 + 1
j = sales.merge(cal, left_on="order_date", right_on="date")
g = j.groupby(["fiscal_year", "fiscal_quarter"])["revenue"].sum().round(0)
for (y, q), v in g.items():
    print(f"FY{y} Q{q}: {int(v)}")
share = j.loc[j["fiscal_year"] == 2026, "revenue"].sum() / j["revenue"].sum() * 100
print(f"share of FY2026: {share:.1f}%")

independent.title: Design the calendar for a real model
independent.prompt: A model has `Sales` (order_date, ship_date) and `Budget` (budget_month) fact tables and the company's year starts in October. Design the date table: columns to include, how you name the fiscal year, how many calendar tables you need and which relationships are active, what you validate before marking it, and the setting for sorting month names in fiscal order.
independent.starter:

independent.solution:
Columns: `date`, `year`, `quarter`, `month_number`, `month_name`, plus `fiscal_year`, `fiscal_quarter`, `fiscal_month` (October is fiscal month 1: `(month - 10) % 12 + 1`) and `fiscal_month_name` if reports show fiscal order. Fiscal naming: state the convention in the model description, for example year in which the fiscal year ends, so Oct 2025 to Sep 2026 is FY2026 (`year + (month >= 10)`).

Relationships: one marked `Calendar`, with the active relationship `Calendar[date]` to `Sales[order_date]`, an inactive one to `Sales[ship_date]` for calculations that need it, and a relationship to `Budget[budget_month]` (budget rows should hold the first day of the month, so they match a date). The calendar must cover all three date columns.

Validation: unique dates, no blanks, contiguous, covers min and max of order, ship and budget dates, whole years. Sorting: sort `month_name` by `month_number`, and sort a fiscal month name column by `fiscal_month`.
rubric: Includes fiscal columns with the right formula for an October start.
Documents the fiscal year naming convention.
One marked calendar with one active and one inactive relationship for Sales, and a relationship for Budget.
Validates the four properties and sorts names by number.

environment.note: Power BI Desktop is Windows-only and has no runtime in this course's browser (Power BI Service runs in a browser). The DAX and M for the calendar and the Desktop steps are shown as text. Every number and every check (validation, sort order, hierarchy totals, fiscal columns) is reproduced with pandas, which runs in the browser. The graded exercises are pandas replicas of the model checks; the written exercises are self-assessed.

checks.question: The Sales table has 237 distinct order dates in 2025. Why is it not enough as a date table?
options: It misses days with no sales and has no year or month columns
It cannot be related to anything
checks.explanation: A date table needs every day, including zero-sales days, and descriptive columns. Sales has 128 missing days in the year.

checks.question: Which of these will make `Mark as date table` fail?
options: A missing day inside the date range
checks.explanation: The date column must be unique, without blanks and contiguous, so one missing day fails the check.

checks.question: Months appear as April, August, December, February. What is the fix?
checks.explanation: The names sort alphabetically. Sort by column uses the number column to set the order.

checks.question: For a fiscal year starting on 1 April, which fiscal month is January?
checks.explanation: (1 - 4) % 12 + 1 = 10: April is month 1, so January is month 10.

checks.question: What does `CALENDAR(DATE(2025,1,1), DATE(2025,12,31))` return in DAX?
options: A one-column table of dates named Date, one row per day
A table with year and month columns
checks.explanation: CALENDAR returns a table with one column named Date. You add year and month columns with ADDCOLUMNS or calculated columns.
